hints.title: Alphabetical Continuity Invariant
hints.text: A string is a valid substring of the infinite wraparound alphabet if adjacent characters satisfy (ord(curr) - ord(prev)) % 26 == 1.

hints.title: Tracking Longest Substring Ending at Each Letter
hints.text: To avoid double counting identical substrings, record only the maximum length of a contiguous valid substring ending at each of the 26 characters.

hints.title: Length Accumulation and Summation
hints.text: Maintain an array of size 26 and curr_len. For each character in s, increment curr_len if continuous, else reset to 1. Update max length for current character, then return sum of the array.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal linear O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space using a 26-element array.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inserting all unique valid substrings into a hash set takes O(N^2) space and time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Max-length per ending character captures all sub-segments without explicit set insertion.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why summing the maximum valid length ending at each letter counts all unique substrings.
